question: After the policy cleanup and clean rebase, is the hosted exact-head evidence sufficient to accept the new command mutation, deduplication, and ledger-publication boundaries?
rationale: The remaining substantive uncertainty is operational: the patch crosses GitHub App tokens, retry behavior, workflow dispatch, and state-repository publication, which focused source tests cannot fully prove.

options.title: Require hosted exact-head proof
options.body: Merge only after a real command run and retry show one mutation path, stable deduplication, bounded requeue behavior, and published immutable receipts.

options.title: Accept focused validation
options.body: Land the clean rebased patch after removing the changelog edit while explicitly accepting residual hosted automation risk.

options.title: Pause the ledger stack
options.body: Keep the draft open if maintainers want the command and downstream repair lifecycle layers reviewed together.

recommendation.title: Require hosted exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Merge only after a real command run and retry show one mutation path, stable deduplication, bounded requeue behavior, and published immutable receipts.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged ledger groundwork and the stacked command/repair lifecycle design, making them the clearest person to assess intended hosted behavior.
